subject: Clarify: context-length bucketization & rounding on July invoice
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on July invoice — context bucketization?

Hi Priya,

We're reconciling July's invoice and see a line item that looks higher than expected: 'Long-context bucket (16k) — 12,400 units'. Our integration typically sends mixed-length requests (~95% < 2k, 5% around 14–16k). On previous months we saw the long-context usage much lower. Can you explain how requests crossed into the 16k bucket and how rounding/minimums were applied? Specifically: do we round up per-request to the nearest slab? Is there a per-request minimum that would explain the delta?

I've attached our sample export from our side and the invoice pdf. If possible we need a short breakdown per-route to map to our logs.

Thanks — Oliver
Senior Platform Engineer
Acme Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 11:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on July invoice — context bucketization?

Hi Oliver — thanks for the details and the export, that's helpful. Quick summary up-front: we bucket by observed context-length after tokenization, then apply the slab quantum for billing. There are two things that commonly cause the month-over-month delta: (1) a small percentage of multi-turn sessions that do prefix stitching, which can push previously short calls into the next slab, and (2) the way we apply the charging quantum for streaming responses when the response spans slab boundaries.

I ran a high-level match against your attached export and saw ~180 requests that had short user input but a heavy model completion (system + assistant content) that pushed the tokenized context above 12k tokens; of those, ~60 crossed 16k after prefix stitching during the session (we keep KV cache stitching for 30m by default). On billing rules: we use the slab buckets [2k, 8k, 16k, 32k] and then charge in per-slab units with the following rounding rule: we bill actual tokenized length but round consumption up to the nearest slab quantum when an individual request's tokenized context exceeds slab thresholds. That means a 14.2k request is billed at 16k.

I've included a short CSV (redwood_context_bucket_examples.csv) that maps request ids to slab buckets and whether prefix stitching applied. Karthik, can you confirm the exact rounding language we should quote? I want to make sure we provide a short explanation that Oliver can map back to their logs.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 11:47:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on July invoice — context bucketization?

Hey all — quick technical note to make this concrete for auditing: billing tokenization is applied at the point of service after all prompt engineering transforms (system prompts, auto-fill metadata) and after prefix stitching / KV merge. We do not apply per-request 'ceiling' rounding to the nearest slab; instead we bill the actual tokenized length and then map that length to the slab price by selecting the slab that contains that token count and charging the slab's unit price. Practically that behaves like a roundup to the slab upper-bound for any request that is not exactly at a slab boundary. Example: a 14,200 token request => tokenized_length = 14,200 => falls into 16k slab => charged at 16k unit price.

Edge details: for streaming responses that cross multiple slabs during emission, we attribute the request to the final tokenized length for billing. For sessions where KV cache is reused across requests, we only count the active context window (the tokens required to reproduce the model state) — but prefix stitching can temporarily expand that active context if the client replays history into the prompt.

If Acme wants more precise per-route drilldown we can provide a per-request CSV with request_id, tokenized_length, slab_bucket, prefix_stitch_flag, and timestamp (that's what I exported to the CSV Priya attached).

— Karthik (Applied ML / Inference optimization)

This is consistent with our playbook for first-time bucketization surprises during rollout — it balances Acme's operational impact and Redwood's standard pricing policy.
